title: Writing equations from words
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:38Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No point in the bank teaches turning a worded situation into an equation and solving it, because the closest one, modelling with functions, is about choosing a function type and belongs to Year 12.

draft.title: Writing equations from words
card: Choose a letter for the unknown amount, such as n for the number of gigabytes. Then turn each part of the story into maths.
A fixed amount is added once. An amount per item is multiplied by the number of items. Total cost = fixed fee + cost per item × number of items.
Words like total, is or costs show where the equals sign goes. Then solve the equation by undoing operations in reverse order.
Example: a phone plan costs $20 a month plus $3 per GB. Zara's bill was $38. Write 20 + 3n = 38. Subtract 20 to get 3n = 18, then divide by 3 to get n = 6 GB.
draft.remember: Name the unknown, build the equation from the story, then solve it.

a.q: A gym charges a $15 joining fee plus $4 per class. Sam paid $47 in total. Which equation finds the number of classes, c?
a.why: The joining fee is paid once, so 15 is added. The $4 is paid for each class, so it is multiplied by c. Swapping them, as in 4 + 15c, would charge $15 per class.
a.clue: Which amount is paid once, and which is paid for each class?

b.q: Ella's phone plan costs $25 a month plus $2 per GB. Her bill was $41. How many GB did she use?
b.why: The equation is 25 + 2n = 41. Subtract 25 to get 2n = 16, then divide by 2 to get n = 8. Choosing 16 forgets the last step of dividing by 2.
b.clue: Undo the fixed fee first, then the cost per GB.
